The chosen pilot is the **Evening Access Pilot** — thirteen Thursday openings coupled with the Northside–Kiln Field late minibus, at **£24,000** (£9,600 evening opening + £14,400 bus subsidy), sitting inside a **£37,500** committed plan with the rest of the envelope left unspent and lapsing. lines.item: Evening opening, 13 weeks (responsible person + utilities + cleaning)
Late bus subsidy: one minibus on the Northside-Kiln Field loop, 13 weeks
Additional Youth Studio sessions: up to 4 per month for the quarter (12 sessions, same £6,500 block price)
Staff training: welcome and access awareness, 2 days
Targeted mailer to priority-neighbourhood households (two dated evenings, booking route)

items.question: Does the plan refuse to generalize the 92% satisfaction figure beyond the people surveyed?
Does the plan explain the Youth Studio fall as a supply/session-frequency change rather than lost interest?
Does the plan treat transport as the active ingredient of the 2023 evening success?
Does the plan avoid repeating the 2022 print campaign as a primary intervention, citing the evidence?
Does the plan respect the capital lead time and the first-floor restriction?
Does the plan stay inside the fixed envelope and use only quoted costs?
Was the revised lift quote (£27,500, 8 weeks, entrance required before evening events over 60) incorporated?
Was the estates survey used, including the awareness finding that contradicts the old board minute?
Did the plan correctly treat the café notice as NOT changing the plan?
Does decisions.json declare concrete round-2 changes?

changes.change: Doubled the Youth Studio block from 2 to 4 additional sessions a month (6 to 12 sessions for the quarter) at the same £6,500.
changes.why: updates/U3 is a written clarification from the partner: its own funding cut halved delivery in June 2024, it holds a 40-name waiting list, and it can supply staff for up to four extra sessions a month at the same £6,500. Round 1 bought only half of what the same money now buys. The £6,500 line and the total are unchanged.

changes.change: Raised the Youth Studio targets from 780 to 1,000 visits and from 120 to 140 monthly unique participants.
changes.why: 18 sessions instead of 12. 1,000 visits is 55.6 per session, a 25% discount to the current 74 per session, because the block is not linear: the first six extra sessions draw on the waitlist, the second six have to fill from the same base. 140 is 115 current participants plus 25 of the 40-name waitlist.

changes.change: Added a hard 60-attendee cap to every evening event, with pre-booking, a door count, a hard stop at 60, a turnaway log, and a new metric (M13).
changes.why: updates/U2 adds a building-control condition: the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor. The entrance is not operable and the repair is capital, so the cap is a licence condition, not a target. The 180-seat hall is no longer the binding capacity.

changes.change: Changed the mailer from one dated evening to two dated evenings with a booking route, reserved half of each mailed date's places for Northside and Kiln Field bookings until 48 hours before, and removed the mailer from the G0 fallback package.
changes.why: Under a 60-attendee cap, a single dated offer risks turning away the estate residents the pilot exists to reach. Two dates spread demand; the reservation protects the priority audience from the cap. The mailer cost is unchanged at £4,200. Because it is now built around two dated pilot evenings, it is not committed if the pilot is not; the fallback is Studio + training (£9,300).

changes.change: Retained the 640 evening-visit target but added a cap-constrained reading rule: attendance plus recorded turnaways counts as the demand floor.
changes.why: 640 is 49.2 per opening across 13 openings (82% of the cap) or 53.3 across 12 programmed sessions (89% of the cap); the 2023 effect of +38% would be 54.9 per session, or 91.4% of the cap. The cap can censor a successful result, so turnaways must be counted and reported alongside attendance rather than treated as an anecdote.

changes.change: Updated the lift everywhere to £27,500 and an 8-week lead, and revised the capital recommendation: the cheapest coherent package containing the lift is now £51,500, £3,500 over the envelope.
changes.why: updates/U2 re-quoted the work and added the 60-attendee condition. Round 1 could describe a lift + evening + bus package at £46,000 that fitted by deleting the Studio; the re-quote removes that option. Lift + evening + bus + Studio is £58,000, £10,000 over. The lift must be a separate capital bid, instructed as early as possible so the 8-week lead does not consume a programme quarter.

changes.change: Revised the assessment's awareness finding from 'awareness is not the binding constraint' to 'awareness is uneven, not absent'.
changes.why: updates/U1 finds that 48% of households across Northside and Kiln Field have never heard of the centre, 37% have heard but never attended, and only 15% have attended at least once. Round 1's claim was based on the 2022 borough print null, which did not measure estate awareness. The 2022 null still stands for borough-wide print; it does not support the stronger claim that awareness is irrelevant.

changes.change: Upgraded the targeted mailer from the weakest line in the budget to the evidenced response to a measured awareness gap, while keeping its week-4 stop rule.
changes.why: updates/U1 gives the mailer a specific audience and a measured gap. It remains a test, not a certainty: the equalities team says it has not tested whether awareness alone converts, and the 2022 package already included a mail-drop that produced no detectable effect. Hence one wave, two dates, and S5 (fewer than 30 registrations means no repeat).

changes.change: Recorded cost as an unaddressed barrier: 22% of aware estate households name cost as the main barrier, and the quoted menu contains no ticket or fare subsidy.
changes.why: updates/U1's barrier split is 57% transport, 22% cost, 11% programme content. The plan can act on transport and awareness, but it cannot invent a subsidy. Recording it prevents the report from claiming that access has been improved across the board.

changes.change: Removed the café equipment refresh from the option set as no longer available, rather than as rejected on merit.
changes.why: updates/U4 defers the refresh to the next financial year and says it is no longer available this quarter. The supplier change has no programming or budget effect and prices to visitors are unchanged. The café was already unfunded, so the revenue plan and total are unchanged.

changes.change: Renamed uncertainty IDs to UNC- to avoid collision with the update file IDs, resolved the old partner-capacity uncertainty, and added new uncertainties for the 60-cap scope and the cost barrier.
changes.why: Updates are numbered U1-U4; the round-1 uncertainties were also U1-U14, which made references ambiguous. UNC-4 is now largely resolved by updates/U3; UNC-3 covers whether the 60 condition catches the Youth Studio; UNC-10 covers cost; UNC-7 now includes cap censoring.

changes.change: Revised cost-effectiveness: Youth Studio about £14 per additional visit (was £25); blended about £59 (was £90); evening unchanged at about £147.
changes.why: The same £6,500 now buys 12 sessions and a target of 476 additional visits rather than 6 sessions and 256. The Studio target is not doubled because the marginal sessions are harder to fill. The evening ratio is unchanged because both its cost and its target are unchanged.

changes.change: Revised stop rule S6, added S7 (cap saturation) and added a cap-breach incident rule (C1).
changes.why: The partner has already confirmed the block in writing, so the old S6 (partner cannot confirm 3 sessions a month) is obsolete; the new failure mode is a delivery shortfall against a block price. The 60 cap creates two new failure modes: saturation, which should trigger the capital case, and breach, which is a licensing incident rather than a missed target.

changes.change: Kept the revenue allocation and the £37,500 total unchanged; the £10,500 headroom still lapses.
changes.why: Every changed item either costs the same (Studio, mailer) or is outside the revenue envelope (lift). No new quoted item became available and the café left the menu. A second mailer wave (£4,200, taking the total to £41,700) was considered and not committed because it would have to be bought before the week-4 result exists. The plan still fits a 15% reduced envelope of £40,800 with £3,300 to spare.

declaredPilot.name: Evening Access Pilot
declaredPilot.why: It remains the only intervention in the pack that has already been tested at this venue, and it was tested in the most informative way available: the 2023 evening programme drew 38% more attendance year-on-year with a minibus, then fell back to pre-pilot level within six weeks of the minibus stopping, with the new estate attendees gone. Same building, same programme, same staff, weeks apart - that isolates transport rather than programme or awareness as the binding constraint. updates/U1 sharpens the case: among estate households that have heard of the centre, 57% name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier, while 48% have never heard of it at all, which is why the pilot pairs transport with a targeted, dated offer. It is also the only instrument that reaches Northside and Kiln Field by construction, because the minibus goes to them and nowhere else, and the only proposal whose failure would teach the board something before it commits to a recurrent transport line. Opening and transport are funded as one unit because funding either alone reproduces a known failure: opening without the bus is the six weeks of 2023 that did not work, and the bus without opening delivers people to a closed door. The pilot now runs under a hard 60-attendee cap until the accessible entrance is operable (updates/U2); it complies by pre-booking, counting at the door, stopping entry at 60 and logging turnaways, and it treats those turnaways as evidence for the separate capital bid rather than as a reason to breach the licence.
target_segments: Estate households that have never heard of the centre (48% of the two estates)
Lapsed Evening Talks attendees from the pre-July-2024 cohort
Public-transport-dependent working adults excluded by the 19:10 last bus
